source_ref: OSF v2zur (CC BY 4.0, as recorded for sibling tables): W1/W2 from C19PRC_UKW1W2_archive_final.sav (md5 cb2ffbf3348cb02736688d7533cc8caa, read in place at itemtext/.cache/c19prc_uk_mcbride_2021_shared/w12/) variable+value labels for W1_C19_Risk1-8 and W2_C19_Risk1-9; W3 from C19PRC_UK_W3_archive_final.sav (md5 c0c028d88079ed72825223b15ee1e332, read in place at itemtext/.cache/c19prc_uk_mcbride_2021_comfort/w3/) labels for W3_C19_Risk1-9. Wording cross-checked against Q87 in 'C19PRC_UKW1 survey questionnaire.pdf' p.48 (image-only, read visually), 'C19PRC_UKW2 survey questionnaire v2.pdf' p.50, and 'C19PRC_UK_W3_Phase_1 questionnaire.pdf' / 'Phase_2 questionnaire.pdf' Q87 (identical in both phases).
note: Item codes are the .sav column names W{w}_C19_RiskN with the wave prefix stripped by data/c19prc_uk_mcbride_2021_build.py (crosswalk key riskbehaviour_c19); items 6-9 are wave_specific and get a _W1/_W2/_W3 suffix because their content changed at W3; W1 has no item 9. Code IS the source column name after prefix strip/suffix, no positional step, no recode or reverse-coding. Each .sav variable label reads '<stem> - <behaviour>'; the behaviour went to item_text verbatim (16/16 identical to the questionnaire grid rows, incl. the W3 trailing '?' on items 7-9 and the US spelling 'Sanitized') and the stem to section_prompt. The stem differs by wave: W1/W2 'To reduce your risk of being infected by the coronavirus COVID-19 have you recently...', W3 'To reduce your risk of being infected by COVID-19, in the past week have you...'. Because it varies, instructions is blank and (following the batch_715 hygiene convention) section _1 = C19_Risk1-5 (pooled W1-W3, statements byte-identical in all three waves, asserted in the build) carries the W1/W2 stem, section _2 = Risk6-8_W1 and Risk6-9_W2 carries the W1/W2 stem, section _3 = Risk6-9_W3 carries the W3 stem. The 2019 W3 responses per pooled item (of 5450: W1 2025, W2 1406, W3 2019) were given under the W3 stem; disclosed in public_note. Items 6-8 _W1 and _W2 have identical wording (split only by the build's wave suffixing); C19_Risk9_W2 and C19_Risk6_W3 are the same behaviour ('Avoided touching your eyes or mouth') under different codes. option_text = the .sav value labels 1=No, 2=Occasionally, 3=Whenever possible, identical for all 26 wave-variables; the W1 Qualtrics questionnaire prints 'Occassionally' (misspelled) with codes 1/2/4, the W2/W3 questionnaires and every .sav label read 'Occasionally', so the .sav spelling was shipped. The OSF 'McBride et al. (2020) measures information.docx' 2.2.7.6 paraphrases this block as 7 items (omits 'Eaten a more balanced diet'), drops 'the coronavirus' from the stem, and appends a 1 'Not at all' .. 4 'Avoided completely' range copied from the preceding Protect block; it contradicts the .sav and questionnaires and was not used. Cross-check (not required for data_labels): .sav per wave x item x resp counts match the live table cell-for-cell, 78/78 (e.g. W1 C19_Risk1 1686/231/108, W3 C19_Risk1 461/756/802, W1 C19_Risk6_W1 839/606/580, C19_Risk9_W3 124/365/1530); live 47025 rows, 2878 ids, wave rows 16200/12654/18171. Every item-wave has all three levels. Study-authored items (measures doc cites public-health guidance, no source instrument); no rights-holder restriction beyond the deposit's CC BY 4.0; no register row applies. English administration.
public_note: Items C19_Risk1-5 pool Waves 1-3: Wave 1-2 respondents were asked 'To reduce your risk of being infected by the coronavirus COVID-19 have you recently...', while the 2019 Wave 3 responses per item were given under 'To reduce your risk of being infected by COVID-19, in the past week have you...'
